problemText: Water can be split by electricity: 2 H₂O → 2 H₂ + O₂. While balancing an equation, which number is a chemist allowed to change?
choices: The subscript 2 inside H₂O, because it counts the hydrogen atoms
The coefficient 2 written in front of H₂O
Either number, as long as the atom totals end up equal
Neither one — a balanced equation is fixed and cannot be adjusted
hints: One number sits in FRONT of a formula and one sits INSIDE it. Only one of them can change without turning the substance into a different chemical.

problemText: Aluminum foil reacts with chlorine gas to form aluminum chloride: Al + Cl₂ → AlCl₃. Which version is balanced with the smallest whole-number coefficients?
choices: Al + 3 Cl → AlCl₃
4 Al + 6 Cl₂ → 4 AlCl₃
2 Al + 3 Cl₂ → 2 AlCl₃
3 Al + 2 Cl₂ → 3 AlCl₃
hints: Tally Al and Cl on both sides of each option before judging it.
Two of the options tally correctly — pick the one whose coefficients share no common factor, and reject any option that split Cl₂ into single Cl atoms.

problemText: A student heats 8.4 g of baking soda in an OPEN dish: 2 NaHCO₃(s) → Na₂CO₃(s) + H₂O(g) + CO₂(g). After heating, the solid left in the dish weighs 5.3 g. What best explains the drop from 8.4 g to 5.3 g?
choices: Gaseous products (water vapor and CO₂) escaped from the open dish, carrying away 3.1 g — mass is still conserved
Heat destroyed 3.1 g of matter, so mass was not conserved in this reaction
The balance must be miscalibrated, because the mass has to read 8.4 g after any reaction
The solid absorbed heat energy, and energy has no mass, so the reading fell
hints: Conservation of mass counts EVERY product, including the ones you cannot see.
Two of the three products are gases and the dish is open — where did they go?

problemText: Hexane, C₆H₁₄, is a solvent that burns completely in oxygen: C₆H₁₄ + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O. Balance this combustion using the smallest whole-number coefficients. What is the coefficient of O₂?
hints: Balance carbon first, then hydrogen, and save oxygen for last because it appears in both products.
With one C₆H₁₄ you get 6 CO₂ and 7 H₂O, which is 12 + 7 = 19 oxygen atoms, so O₂ takes 19/2 — then multiply every coefficient by 2 to clear the fraction.

problemText: Slaked lime neutralizes phosphoric acid: Ca(OH)₂ + H₃PO₄ → Ca₃(PO₄)₂ + H₂O. Which version is balanced with the smallest whole-number coefficients?
choices: Ca(OH)₂ + H₃PO₄ → Ca₃(PO₄)₂ + H₂O
3 Ca(OH)₂ + 2 H₃PO₄ → Ca₃(PO₄)₂ + 3 H₂O
6 Ca(OH)₂ + 4 H₃PO₄ → 2 Ca₃(PO₄)₂ + 12 H₂O
3 Ca(OH)₂ + 2 H₃PO₄ → Ca₃(PO₄)₂ + 6 H₂O
hints: PO₄ survives the reaction intact, so count it as a single block instead of atom by atom; do the same for calcium, then finish with hydrogen.
Ca₃(PO₄)₂ pins 3 Ca and 2 PO₄ on the left. That puts 6 H from the hydroxides and 6 H from the acid on the left — 12 H total, so how many H₂O must the right side have?

problemText: Ethanol, C₂H₅OH, burns in a fuel blend: C₂H₅OH + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O. Which line is balanced with the smallest whole-number coefficients?
choices: 2 C₂H₅OH + 7 O₂ → 4 CO₂ + 6 H₂O
C₂H₅OH + 3 O₂ → 2 CO₂ + 3 H₂O
C₂H₅OH + 2 O₂ → 2 CO₂ + 3 H₂O
2 C₂H₅OH + 6 O₂ → 4 CO₂ + 6 H₂O
hints: Ethanol already carries one oxygen atom of its own — that O must be counted on the reactant side along with the O₂.
Two of these options tally correctly on every element; the winner is the one whose coefficients share no common factor.

problemText: Aluminum is produced industrially by passing electricity through molten aluminum oxide: 2 Al₂O₃ → 4 Al + 3 O₂. How should this reaction be classified?
choices: Combustion — O₂ appears in the equation
Synthesis — aluminum and oxygen are combining
Decomposition — a single compound breaks into two simpler substances
Single replacement — oxygen takes the place of aluminum
hints: Count the pieces before you look at the formulas: how many separate reactants are there?

problemText: Hard water is softened by the reaction K₂CO₃(aq) + CaCl₂(aq) → CaCO₃(s) + 2 KCl(aq). How should it be classified?
choices: Single replacement — calcium takes the place of potassium
Double replacement — two compounds trade partners and CaCO₃ leaves as a solid
Synthesis — a solid is built from two solutions
Decomposition — the potassium carbonate falls apart
hints: First check whether either reactant is a lone ELEMENT. Are K₂CO₃ and CaCl₂ elements or compounds?
Two compounds in, two compounds out, with K and Ca having exchanged partners. Which pattern is that?

problemText: Which of these is a combustion reaction?
choices: 2 H₂O₂ → 2 H₂O + O₂
CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂
Na₂SO₄ + BaCl₂ → BaSO₄ + 2 NaCl
2 C₂H₂ + 5 O₂ → 4 CO₂ + 2 H₂O
hints: Combustion needs O₂ going IN as a reactant, plus a fuel — not O₂ coming out as a product.
Look for the equation whose reactants are a hydrocarbon and oxygen gas, and whose only products are CO₂ and H₂O.

problemText: Here are five balanced reactions. (1) 2 Na + 2 H₂O → 2 NaOH + H₂. (2) HNO₃ + KOH → KNO₃ + H₂O. (3) 2 Al + 3 Br₂ → 2 AlBr₃. (4) BaCl₂ + Na₂SO₄ → BaSO₄ + 2 NaCl. (5) 2 HgO → 2 Hg + O₂. How many of these five are DOUBLE REPLACEMENT reactions? Type your answer as a number.
hints: Double replacement needs exactly TWO reactants and no lone element anywhere in the equation.
Reactions 1 and 3 each start with a lone element, and reaction 5 has only one reactant. Count what survives.

problemText: Baking soda releases gas in an oven: 2 NaHCO₃ → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂. How should this reaction be classified?
choices: Decomposition — one reactant breaks apart into three simpler products
Combustion — CO₂ and H₂O are both produced
Double replacement — the sodium and the hydrogen swap partners
Synthesis — sodium carbonate is built up out of smaller pieces
hints: Do not pattern-match on the familiar CO₂ and H₂O. Count the reactants first.
Combustion requires O₂ as a reactant. Is there any O₂ on the left-hand side here?

problemText: Classify all three reactions: (i) 2 C₆H₁₄ + 19 O₂ → 12 CO₂ + 14 H₂O, (ii) H₂SO₄ + 2 NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2 H₂O, (iii) 3 Zn + 2 FeCl₃ → 3 ZnCl₂ + 2 Fe. Which statement is entirely correct?
choices: (i) synthesis, (ii) double replacement, (iii) single replacement
(i) combustion, (ii) neutralization, which is its own sixth category and not a replacement, (iii) single replacement
(i) combustion, (ii) double replacement (specifically a neutralization), (iii) single replacement
(i) combustion, (ii) double replacement, (iii) double replacement — the two chlorides change places
hints: Take them one at a time with the count-the-pieces test, then check whether any special name also applies.
Acid + base → salt + water is a double replacement whose escape product happens to be water; and in (iii) Zn enters as a lone element, which rules out double replacement.

problemText: Activity series excerpt, most reactive to least: K > Na > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > H > Cu > Ag > Au. Which of these metals will NOT bubble when dropped into hydrochloric acid, HCl(aq)?
choices: Zn
Mg
Ag
Fe
hints: Hydrogen is the acid line: metals ABOVE H hand their electrons to H⁺ and release H₂ gas, while metals below H cannot.

problemText: A strip of aluminum metal is placed in zinc nitrate solution, Zn(NO₃)₂. Activity series excerpt: K > Na > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > H > Cu > Ag. Aluminum forms Al³⁺ and nitrate is NO₃⁻. Which line correctly gives the products?
choices: Al(NO₃)₃ + Zn
Al(NO₃)₂ + Zn — the subscript 2 carries over from Zn(NO₃)₂
AlNO₃ + Zn — one aluminum pairs with one nitrate
No reaction — aluminum ranks below zinc on the series
hints: Two checks come first: is Al above Zn on the series, and does the free metal take the metal slot?
Build the product from charges alone — Al³⁺ paired with NO₃⁻ needs however many nitrates it takes to reach a neutral compound, regardless of the subscript in Zn(NO₃)₂.

problemText: Solubility facts: all nitrates are soluble, and all Na⁺ and K⁺ salts are soluble; most sulfates are soluble EXCEPT BaSO₄, PbSO₄, and CaSO₄; all common chlorides are soluble except AgCl and PbCl₂. Which pair of solutions produces a precipitate when mixed?
choices: NaNO₃(aq) + KCl(aq)
Ba(NO₃)₂(aq) + Na₂SO₄(aq)
K₂SO₄(aq) + NaCl(aq)
NaNO₃(aq) + K₂SO₄(aq)
hints: For each pair, first write the two products a partner swap would make, then look each one up in the solubility facts.
Three of the pairs can only produce nitrates or Na⁺/K⁺ salts, and those are all soluble. Which pair can make something that is not?

problemText: Activity series excerpt: Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > H > Cu > Ag > Au. A student is asked what happens when silver wire is placed in zinc nitrate solution and writes 2 Ag + Zn(NO₃)₂ → 2 AgNO₃ + Zn, pointing out that the equation is balanced. Which evaluation is correct?
choices: Correct — the equation balances, which shows the reaction happens
Incorrect — the silver formula should be Ag₂NO₃ so that the charges work out
Incorrect — silver can displace only nonmetals, never another metal
Incorrect — no reaction occurs, because Ag ranks below Zn on the series
hints: A balanced equation is never evidence that a reaction actually runs — only the activity series decides that.
The free metal here is silver. Find both metals on the list: is the free one ranked above or below the one locked in the compound?

problemText: Calcium metal is added to aluminum nitrate solution, Al(NO₃)₃. Activity series excerpt: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > H > Cu > Ag. Calcium forms Ca²⁺, aluminum forms Al³⁺, and nitrate is NO₃⁻. Predict the products, balance the equation, and state the coefficient of Al(NO₃)₃. Type your answer as a number.
hints: Ca sits above Al, so the reaction runs. Build the products from charges: Ca²⁺ with NO₃⁻ gives Ca(NO₃)₂, and the displaced aluminum leaves as neutral Al.
Three Ca(NO₃)₂ units hold six nitrate groups, so the aluminum nitrate on the left must supply six as well — and each Al(NO₃)₃ carries three.

problemText: Activity series excerpt: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > H > Cu > Ag. A student predicts the reaction of magnesium metal with hydrochloric acid and writes Mg + HCl → MgCl + H. Which statement identifies ALL the errors and gives the correct equation?
choices: The only error is the balancing; the correct equation is Mg + 2 HCl → MgCl + 2 H
The formulas are fine, but the reaction does not run, because Mg ranks below H on the series
Two formula errors: magnesium forms Mg²⁺ so the product is MgCl₂, and the hydrogen leaves as the diatomic gas H₂ — the correct equation is Mg + 2 HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂
The products MgCl₂ and H₂ are right, but the reaction still does not run, because no metal reacts with a dilute acid
hints: Check the formulas before you check the balance: what charge does magnesium form, and what chloride formula does that force?
Hydrogen released from an acid comes off as a gas — and gaseous hydrogen is one of the diatomic elements, never a lone H atom.

problemText: Bromine exists as the pure element Br₂. What is the oxidation number of each bromine atom in Br₂?
choices: −1, because bromine usually ends up as Br⁻
+2, because there are two atoms bonded together
hints: Rule 1 of oxidation numbers: an atom in a PURE element is assigned zero, no matter how many atoms the molecule holds.

problemText: Sulfuric acid, H₂SO₄, is neutral overall. Using the rules that hydrogen is +1 and each oxygen is −2, what is the oxidation number of the sulfur atom?
hints: The oxidation numbers of all seven atoms must sum to 0, because the compound carries no overall charge.
Two hydrogens give +2 and four oxygens give 4 × (−2) = −8, a running total of −6. What must sulfur contribute?

problemText: Aluminum foil dropped into copper(II) chloride solution reacts: 2 Al + 3 CuCl₂ → 2 AlCl₃ + 3 Cu. Which species is OXIDIZED?
choices: Al — its oxidation number rises from 0 to +3
Cu — its oxidation number moves from +2 to 0
Cl — it changes partners, moving from copper to aluminum
Nothing is oxidized, because no oxygen appears anywhere in the reaction
hints: Assign numbers first: Al and Cu on their own are pure elements (0), while Cu is +2 in CuCl₂ and Al is +3 in AlCl₃.
Oxidation is LOSS of electrons, which shows up as the oxidation number going UP.

problemText: The dichromate ion, Cr₂O₇²⁻, is the orange ion used in some lab oxidizers. Each oxygen is −2 and the ion carries an overall charge of 2−. What is the oxidation number of EACH chromium atom? Type your answer as a number (write a negative answer like -2).
hints: For a polyatomic ion the oxidation numbers sum to the ION'S CHARGE, which is −2 here, not to zero.
Seven oxygens contribute 7 × (−2) = −14, so the two chromium atoms together must contribute +12. Divide by 2 for a single atom.

problemText: Zinc powder stirred into iron(III) chloride solution reacts: 3 Zn + 2 FeCl₃ → 3 ZnCl₂ + 2 Fe. Which species is the REDUCING agent?
choices: Fe³⁺ — it is the species that gets reduced, so it must be the reducing agent
Cl⁻ — it carries the transferred charge from the iron over to the zinc
ZnCl₂ — the product is where the transferred electrons end up
Zn — it is oxidized from 0 to +2, and the electrons it gives away are what reduce the iron
hints: Assign the numbers: Zn goes 0 → +2, Fe goes +3 → 0, and chloride stays −1 on both sides.
The agent labels are always crossed: the species that is OXIDIZED is the reducing agent, because it supplies the electrons that reduce its partner.

problemText: Oxidation-number rules: a pure element is 0; a monatomic ion equals its charge; hydrogen is +1; oxygen is −2 EXCEPT in peroxides such as H₂O₂, where it is −1; the numbers sum to the overall charge. Which of these reactions is NOT a redox reaction?
choices: 2 H₂O₂ → 2 H₂O + O₂
HNO₃ + KOH → KNO₃ + H₂O
2 NaBr + Cl₂ → 2 NaCl + Br₂
2 C₄H₁₀ + 13 O₂ → 8 CO₂ + 10 H₂O
hints: A reaction is redox only if at least ONE element's oxidation number differs between the reactant side and the product side.

Do not skip the peroxide: oxygen starts at −1 in H₂O₂ and ends at −2 in water and 0 in O₂, so that one does change. In the acid-base pair, check H, N, K, and O one at a time and watch them all hold still.
